- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates in low-sentiment periods; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment <0.33 for 3+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often lags; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
